title: 预算越紧：黑五支出反增5.4%，钱到底花去哪了
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: Stretched US consumers headed into Black Friday with strict budgets.
segments.zh: 手头紧张的美国消费者带着严格预算迎接黑色星期五。

segments.en: Yet, total holiday spending is still expected to climb 5.4% this year.
segments.zh: 然而，今年假日总支出预计仍将增长5.4%。

segments.en: With Americans projected to spend nearly $13 billion online on Black Friday deals alone.
segments.zh: 仅黑色星期五促销，美国人网上消费预计就将接近130亿美元。

segments.en: Despite high fuel costs and lingering inflation, shoppers aren't sitting this season out.
segments.zh: 尽管燃料成本高企、通胀持续，消费者并未缺席这个购物季。

segments.en: They are simply getting more strategic. According to PWC, 40% of consumers are hunting for resale and vintage deals.
segments.zh: 他们只是变得更讲究策略。普华永道称，40%的消费者在寻找转售和复古商品优惠。

segments.en: While others are trimming their gift list or swapping tack for screen-free gifts.
segments.zh: 其他人则在缩减礼物清单，或将实物礼品换成无屏幕礼物。

segments.en: Recent widespread tech outages across banks and flight systems also sparked a wave of proper buying for generators and bottled water at Walmart and Costco.
segments.zh: 近期银行和航班系统的大范围技术故障，也引发了在沃尔玛和好市多抢购发电机和瓶装水的风潮。

segments.en: A cautious mindset trickling into holiday shopping. Coals and Dollar Tree are even drawing in higher-income bargain hunters, with expanded $3 to $20 gift sections.
segments.zh: 谨慎心态正蔓延至假日购物。Coals和Dollar Tree甚至吸引了高收入淘便宜货者，扩大了3至20美元的礼品区。

segments.en: As Dollar Tree CEO put it, shoppers are cherishing value and buying closer to need.
segments.zh: 正如Dollar Tree首席执行官所说，消费者珍视价值，按需购买。
